I'm proposing three body changes, one each for flag, heart and treasure. None has been trialled yet, so all the numbers below are my geometry estimates. Each change is tried on its own; one is kept only if it gains a group and the two held groups (activate and mermaids) still pass.

**1. Flag: shorter frame plus a leaning band mast (most likely to work).** The mast I proposed last time only failed because it didn't fit the box folded: 14.3 in long against the 12 in limit.
- Shortening the frame from 11 to 7 in makes room for the lean. With four 8 in tubes leaning 28°, I estimate the folded size at about 11.6 in long and 15.7 in tall, inside the 12 x 18 in limits.
- Extended, the mast is 27.5 in long. Its top lands about 12.9 in ahead of the robot's front and 32 in up, so the robot parks with its front near 24.7 in. That is outside the fortress wall at 27.6 in and past the merfolk, so the push bar still knocks them over on the same drive.
- It uses four of the five rubber bands and no motor or piston; the existing release lets it go when the robot parks.
- Cost: four aluminium tubes, $10.

**2. Heart: hook boom with a shorter swing.** Last time this was refused because the piston rod lined up too closely with the boom (16°, under the 20° minimum) over a 135° swing.
- Swinging down only 10° instead of 45° cuts the swing to 100°. That should keep the rod angle above 20°, though the brief doesn't give the piston mounting, so this may fail the same way.
- In the last match the push bar shut the chest lid, so the realistic target is pulling the whole chest back (32 points) rather than the heart (61).
- It uses one of the two free pistons and costs $3.50.

**3. Treasure: sorting chute resized to fit (riskiest).** I made the change the refusal suggested: raised the trough's low end from 7 to 11 in and shortened and flattened the side troughs (8 in at 22°).
- On my estimate the side troughs now end about 1.9 in above the floor and the chute folds to about 17.2 in tall. Both figures depend on extra height losses I could only infer from the last refusal.
- If the side troughs fold up above the deck, they would reach 16 in and it may be refused for size again.
- The troughs end at about ±13.4 in sideways, short of the mounds at ±15 in, so pieces may not land on the mounds.

iterations.notes:
I've proposed three variations of one change for this final iteration: a gate_chute cannon on a shorter frame. All three could fail, and the trials decide what's kept.

**What I chose and why.** The only cannon that ran before scored nothing: the balls missed the port and a rule was broken. My reading, which no trial has shown yet, is that its exit stopped about 2 in past the fortress edge, which is too short. Length is the limit: the 22 in bar forces the robot's length onto the box's 12 in side, and the past folds fit folded length = frame + reach + 0.3 in. So the only way to reach further is a shorter frame. Every proposal keeps frame + reach at 11.5 in (11.8 in folded) and varies the frame (6.5 to 7.5 in), the reach (4.0 to 5.0 in) and the exit height (9 to 12 in) to bracket where the port is. The rule break was most likely the chute still reaching into the fortress at 40 s. That is System 1's job to fix: it already drives back, and it must retract the piston before 40 s.

**Held groups at risk.** Neither held group is safe by inspection:
- **Leaving the dock:** 7.5, 7 and 6.5 in are all shorter than any frame tried. Frame 8.5 with this same chute kept both held groups in iteration 5. The 6.5 in frame carries the most risk of the robot tipping forward on braking.
- **Toppling the merfolk:** the 22 in bar at 7.5 in is unchanged, but this group was lost in several earlier trials where the bar hadn't changed either.

**Cost:** about $1 (one hinge), 2 days' lead time and 66 g of PLA (66 machine minutes) for any of the three.

**What I left out, with reasons:**
- **Flag:** a boom that folds into the 12 x 22 x 18 in box can't reach 10.8 in forward to the pole and also put the flag's top 24 in up. The band mast reached the pole but never met a face square to it, and two of its later variants lost the merfolk.
- **Heart:** the 22 in bar has to cross x = 20 to topple the merfolk, and the chest sits at 19.9 to 23.1 in. In the full-match trial the bar shut the lid and knocked the heart to (25.9, 6.7). The two hook-boom attempts were also scored as a shut lid.
- **Treasure:** the sorting chute's blade missed the figures. Its height can't be fitted without knowing the height of the fortress top.

**Match task:** reaching 174 points is out of reach this iteration. A working cannon would add at most 36 to the current 35.
